es: Distinguir imply, infer, suggest e indicate: quién da a entender, quién deduce y con qué fuerza los datos apuntan a una conclusión.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo con tres pistas, una conclusión y una alternativa descartada.

answer.text: The bakery has been closed for five days, and there are three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front has new paint. Third, someone saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. These clues suggest that the bakery is not closing for good: it is probably having a renovation or moving to a bigger place. Of course, each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case. We can rule out the alternative that the owner has left, because of the new sign. I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.
accepted: The bakery has been closed for five days, and there are three clues. First, there is a delivery van at the door. Second, the front has new paint. Third, someone saw the owner with a new sign yesterday. These clues suggest that the bakery is not closing for good: it is probably having a renovation or moving to a bigger place. Of course, each clue on its own is weak, but together they make a strong case. We can rule out the alternative that the owner has left, because of the new sign. I will ask him tomorrow to be sure.

The bakery has been shut for five days. I can see a van outside, fresh paint on the wall and a new sign in the owner's hand. Together, these clues point to a renovation, although I may be wrong. The bakery is unlikely to be closing for good, because nobody buys a new sign and paints a wall before leaving. I can rule out that alternative, and I will check with the owner tomorrow.

prompt.es: Escribe el caso: dos hipótesis, un descarte y una conclusión con pruebas.

answer.text: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two theories. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. Both ideas are possible at first, but only one fits the evidence. The door was locked all night, so a stranger can't have come in. Also, the cabinet is not broken, which points to someone with a key. The cleaner has a key and came yesterday, so the cleaner must have moved the trophy. I can't be completely sure, so we should ask the cleaner first.
accepted: The trophy is missing from the cabinet, and I have two theories. First, a stranger might have taken it during the night. Second, the cleaner could have moved it. Both ideas are possible at first, but only one fits the evidence. The door was locked all night, so a stranger can't have come in. Also, the cabinet is not broken, which points to someone with a key. The cleaner has a key and came yesterday, so the cleaner must have moved the trophy. I can't be completely sure, so we should ask the cleaner first.

We have two possible explanations for the missing trophy. A stranger may have taken it, or the cleaner might have moved it. A stranger cannot have taken it, because the door was locked all night and the cabinet is not broken. Since the cleaner has a key and came yesterday, the most likely explanation is that the cleaner moved it. I am not certain, so we should ask tomorrow.

Pistas: (1) el armario no está roto; (2) la puerta del aula estuvo cerrada con llave toda la noche; (3) la persona de la limpieza tiene una llave y vino ayer. Escribe en inglés (70–150 palabras): propón dos hipótesis con might o could (un extraño y la persona de la limpieza), descarta una con can't have y explica por qué, y concluye con evidencia (must have o probably).
